# m0serve

> A WSGI and ASGI server written in Mojo: `pip install m0serve`, no Mojo
> toolchain, no dependencies, nothing fetched at install. Its distinguishing
> capability: held SSE and WebSocket connections gated by plain synchronous
> views (Django, Flask, ...), with cross-worker publish, needing neither
> Channels nor Redis nor a second process. On throughput it is ahead of
> uvicorn with uvloop on bare ASGI and on the fast-request tail under mixed
> load, and behind Granian on bare WSGI; the benchmarks page has the
> numbers, each rendered from a dated artifact.

Platforms: macOS arm64 (13+), Linux x86_64 and aarch64 (glibc; the exact
floor is in the wheel filename, and pip refuses rather than crashes on older
systems). CPython 3.10-3.14; free-threaded builds run WSGI only. No Windows,
no musl, no TLS/HTTP2 (terminate at a proxy).

## Operating contract

- `m0serve MODULE[:ATTR]` serves WSGI or ASGI, detected from the object.
  Bare `MODULE` tries `MODULE.asgi:application`, `MODULE.wsgi:application`,
  `MODULE:app`, `MODULE.main:app`.
- Zero-config topology follows the protocol: WSGI gets one loop with a pool
  of `min(cores, 8)` handler threads; ASGI gets an asyncio executor.
  `--workers N` preforks; `--mount PREFIX=SPEC` hosts several applications
  in one process, each in its own mode; `--threads N` is free-threaded
  CPython only and WSGI only (an ASGI app there is refused with exit 78).
- Flags are strict and named in `m0serve --help`; flags override `M0_*`
  environment variables, which override defaults.
- Refusals explain themselves on stderr and name the fix. Exit 2 is usage,
  1 is a startup failure, 78 is a configuration the interpreter cannot run.
  `--version` prints `m0serve X.Y.Z`.
- `m0serve --doctor [OPTIONS] [MODULE]` prints one JSON object and starts
  nothing: platform, interpreter, the application spec discovery chose and
  its protocol, the resolved topology, and a `checks` array where every
  failure carries `detail`, `fix` and `exit`. It exits with the code
  `m0serve` itself would exit with for the same arguments.
- `--health-path /health` answers 200 in the server, before Python.
- Realtime: a view's response with `M0-Hold: stream|websocket` and
  `M0-Channel: NAME` converts the connection to a held subscription;
  `from m0serve import m0pub; m0pub.publish(channel, data)` reaches every
  subscriber on every worker. Inbound WebSocket messages arrive as POSTs to
  `/ws/message` with `M0-Channel`/`M0-Slot`/`M0-Opcode` headers. `--realtime`
  composes with `--blocking-threads` and `--mount`; it is refused only where
  nothing could take a hold (an ASGI-only server).
- `--static PREFIX=DIR` serves files from the server with sendfile, ETags
  and byte ranges; a miss falls through to the application.
- SIGTERM drains in-flight work and exits 0; the server runs as PID 1
  correctly.

## Start here

- [Quickstart](QUICKSTART.md): live multi-tab sync from one file of sync
  Django, in five steps. CI runs every fenced block.
- [After the quickstart](docs/QUICKSTART_NEXT.md): the same application
  under two workers, in Flask, and under gunicorn.
- [Running m0serve](docs/RUNNING.md): flags, modes, what to put in front of
  it, shutdown and exit codes.
- [Capabilities](docs/SPEC.md): one row per capability with the CI gate
  that proves it; `docs/spec.json` is the same data. `verified` means a
  gate runs on the stated cadence, not that the capability is correct.
- [Benchmarks](docs/BENCHMARKS.md): throughput and tail latency against
  gunicorn, uvicorn and Granian, from dated artifacts, including where this
  server loses.
- The realtime example the quickstart builds on, as a project:
  [apps/django_realtime](apps/django_realtime/).

## The Mojo stack: operating contract

Preview. A second package, `m0`, for writing the application itself in
Mojo on the framework m0serve is built from: one compiled binary, no Python
at run time. `m0` is pure Python and versioned apart from m0serve. Toolchain
platforms: macOS arm64, glibc Linux x86_64 and aarch64.

- `uvx m0 new NAME [--template views|live]` writes a project and needs no
  toolchain and no network. Inside it every command is `uv run m0 ...`;
  `uv sync` installs the two exact pins, `m0` and the one `mojo` it was
  tested on. `m0` runs the `mojo` in its own environment, never `PATH`'s,
  and refuses any other version. There is no override.
- `m0 build` compiles `src/server.mojo` to `bin/server` by rename, so a
  running server is never written over; `m0 build --release` makes a
  relocatable `dist/` for the platform's baseline CPU. A build needs a C
  compiler named `cc`. `m0 test` runs `test/test_*.mojo` and needs none; it
  is several times faster than a build, so logic belongs where a test
  reaches it. A build does not diagnose a function nothing calls.
- `m0 dev [-- HOST_ARGS]` builds, serves and rebuilds on save. The old
  server answers until a build succeeds; a failed build changes nothing.
- `m0 doctor --json [-- HOST_ARGS]` prints one JSON object: every toolchain
  check, then the binary's own report. Parse it; do not scrape stderr.
- `m0 image` is `docker build -f deploy/Dockerfile` and then the image's
  `/app/about.json` (`"python":false`, the CPU compiled for, bytes) as the
  last line of stdout. It needs docker and a committed `uv.lock`.
- Exit codes, from `m0` and from the binary: 0; 1 the tool that ran failed;
  2 a command line that cannot be read; 78 a refusal, one line naming the
  fix. Read the line; do not retry.
- The binary: flag over `M0_*` variable over default. `--workers N` forks,
  `--threads N` is loops in one process (not both above 1),
  `--blocking-threads N` is a handler pool behind each loop. `--doctor`
  prints the resolved configuration as the last line of stdout, binds
  nothing, and exits with the code serving would. SIGTERM drains and
  exits 0.
- A view is a free function `(req, params, state) raises -> HTTPResponse`
  in a `Views[S]` table: `add_read` borrows the state, `add_write` takes it
  `mut`, `add_loop` has none and runs on the event loop. No middleware, no
  decorators: a guard is an early return. State held in one process
  declares `max_workers() -> 1`, and a second worker is then refused.
- `Fragment[Htmx]` (htmx 4) or `Fragment[Datastar]` generates every swap
  attribute from the fragment's root id; never type one by hand. `text` and
  `attr` escape, `raw` does not. `page_or_fragment` answers a document or
  the bare fragment from the request headers and sets `Vary`. Routes are
  `comptime` constants given to the table and to `url_for`.
- A request-derived `String` may not be UTF-8: never slice one with
  `s[byte=a:b]`; use `String(unsafe_from_utf8=s.as_bytes()[a:b])`.
- Not built: a template engine, middleware, an ORM, multipart parsing, a
  session store, password hashing.
- A scaffolded project's `AGENTS.md` is this contract at full length, and
  `uv run m0 include` prints where the framework's source is installed.
